user_questions.question: The org has no concept of support-agent tier (no tier role, profile, permission set, group, or User field; no human agent users yet). How should 'below Tier 2' be defined? Options: (A) Recommended: a new dedicated Tier 2 permission set grants Read on Refund__c.Amount__c, everyone else (Tier 1) has no grant; (B) use roles CustomerSupportNorthAmerica/CustomerSupportInternational (roles control sharing, not field visibility); (C) add a tier field on User and drive visibility from it (needs code or dynamic visibility, weaker).
user_questions.simulated_answer: Amount hidden for Tier 1 agents; visible to a Tier 2 permission set.

skill_friction: Step 5 says to predict the answer and decide if 'no preference' is expected, but here the persona fork (how Tier 2 is represented) was genuinely needed; the skill gives no guidance on whether a missing persona representation (no tier concept in org) counts as 'which persona' or as implementation (how to build). I treated it as an intent question.

AskCoworker repeatedly labels facts '[Verified: prior session]' and invents components (AgentActionsTest); the rule to treat these as untraceable is clear but the volume forced re-verifying nearly everything.

AskCoworker I proposed a separate 'PermissionSetFieldSecurity' row for a field permission inside a permission set; spec-format says not to fold dependent parts but does not say field/object permissions are part of the PermissionSet component. I merged them; explicit guidance would help.

Design-rules 'a security fix must not be bypassable by the same actor' vs. Apex/flow paths that echo caller-supplied values: no guidance on whether echoing back a value the caller supplied counts as a bypass. I treated it as non-blocking proposal.

org-verification.md says users with View All Data still see fields without FLS; this is at odds with typical platform behavior (View All Data does not override FLS in most contexts), so I stated it as documented behavior per the reference but it may be inaccurate.
